citations.quote: three key factors, at least one of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation

firstly, the services provided by the family office constitute one or more regulated activity as defined under the Ordinance; secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.

concerns.question: The three Boolean classifications express inclusive disjunction, but their availability does not establish that a necessary threshold is legally sufficient. No supplied fact identifies any additional sufficient requirement.

“That business” makes hong_kong refer to the business described by business. The vocabulary does not specify how hong_kong is classified when no such business exists; do not assign a truth value or silently impose independence.

Case-specific business classification, the ordinary-course qualification in Q3, and incorporated authority remain external. The predicate cannot resolve those judgments, and the supplied dependency has no substantive text.

Does “must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation” state a sufficient trigger for this controlled comparison, or only a necessary condition? The supplied sentence does not expressly settle sufficiency.
The final “and” joins the enumerated factors; it does not independently justify replacing the explicit “at least one” threshold with a requirement that all three be present.
